pageTypes.title: Landing Page
pageTypes.description: Channel focused mentors and vocabulary to keep a single conversion goal honest.

prompts.name: Channel Oli Gardner
prompts.shortDescription: Conversion-obsessed cofounder of Unbounce who coined the attention ratio mantra.
prompts.prompt: Act as Oli Gardner and strip this landing page brief to one CTA. Label each remaining block as Goal or Noise, rewrite copy and layout notes so everything marches toward that single action.

prompts.name: Channel Joanna Wiebe
prompts.shortDescription: Punchy conversion copy from the Copyhackers playbook - clear, specific, and momentum heavy.
prompts.prompt: Act as Joanna Wiebe critiquing this hero. Deliver a plain-stated headline, a subhead that amplifies value, and a CTA verb that signals momentum. Keep every sentence rooted in proof.

prompts.name: Channel Peep Laja
prompts.shortDescription: CXL founder who demands testable hypotheses and brutal focus on the primary KPI.
prompts.prompt: Act as Peep Laja reviewing this landing page. Restate the primary KPI, eliminate elements that cannot justify their impact on it, and rewrite the offer so it reads like a hypothesis you can instrument.

principles.title: One page, one goal
principles.definition: Every campaign page exists to drive a single conversion. Anything that does not support that action gets demoted or removed.
principles.whyItMatters: A 1:1 attention ratio keeps visitors from leaking to low-intent pages and lifts conversion rates across channels.
principles.example: Hide the global nav and keep only “Book teardown” as the actionable link.

principles.title: Clarity beats clever
principles.definition: Headlines answer what the product is and why it matters before trying to be witty.
principles.whyItMatters: Visitors bounce within seconds if they have to decode metaphors.
principles.example: Swap “Give your funnels wings” for “Build CRO-ready landing pages in hours.”

principles.title: Attention ratio
principles.definition: For each campaign, there should be one primary CTA for every traffic source. No side quests.
principles.whyItMatters: Additional links dilute focus and reduce conversions from paid acquisition.
principles.example: Move Docs, Careers, and Blog links to a post-conversion email instead of the hero.

principles.title: Visual hierarchy
principles.definition: Typography, spacing, and contrast guide the eye from headline to subhead to CTA without distractions.
principles.whyItMatters: When everything looks equal, nothing gets read.
principles.example: Use a bold 48px headline, a muted 18px subhead, and a high-contrast CTA button.

principles.title: Message match
principles.definition: The landing page headline and imagery should echo the ad or email that drove the click.
principles.whyItMatters: Consistency prevents pogo-sticking back to search results and keeps Quality Scores high.
principles.example: If the ad touts “3-hour teardown,” the hero headline repeats it verbatim.

principles.title: Friction reducers
principles.definition: Microcopy, trust badges, and slim forms reduce perceived effort at the decision point.
principles.whyItMatters: Even motivated visitors hesitate if they fear spam, long calls, or complex onboarding.
principles.example: Add “No deck needed” plus SOC2 badge beside the CTA form.

principles.title: Above the fold logic
principles.definition: The first screen answers what it is, who it is for, proof it works, and the way to start.
principles.whyItMatters: Paid clicks often bounce before scrolling, so the fold has to earn the next swipe.
principles.example: Hero headline + subhead, logo strip, and CTA all visible without scroll on desktop.

principles.title: Section flow
principles.definition: Order sections Problem → Value → Proof → Action so belief builds with each scroll.
principles.whyItMatters: Randomized content forces context switching and erodes momentum.
principles.example: Place testimonials after value props and before pricing to answer “will this work for me?”

pageTypes.title: Design
pageTypes.description: Translate CRO strategy into layout, typography, and brand systems that still protect the CTA.

prompts.name: Channel Dieter Rams
prompts.shortDescription: Ten principles purist laser-focused on calm grids, purposeful contrast, and generous whitespace.
prompts.prompt: Act as Dieter Rams. Audit this layout for "less but better": define the grid, spacing scale, and contrast rules that keep the CTA dominant while letting proof elements breathe.

prompts.name: Channel Paula Scher
prompts.shortDescription: Pentagram legend who marries bold typography with strategic storytelling.
prompts.prompt: Act as Paula Scher shaping this landing page. Rebuild the hierarchy with typography, color, and iconography that dramatize the story beats yet still funnel attention to the CTA.

prompts.name: Channel Brad Frost
prompts.shortDescription: Atomic design evangelist who inventories tokens, components, and templates before pixels.
prompts.prompt: Act as Brad Frost building a system for this experience. List the atoms, molecules, and templates, spell out responsive behavior, and note the rules that protect accessibility and CTA clarity.

principles.title: Hierarchy is a system
principles.definition: Spacing, type scale, and contrast ladder up to a predictable rhythm so the eye lands exactly where we want.
principles.whyItMatters: Inconsistent hierarchy forces readers to hunt for the CTA and derails the story arc.
principles.example: Lock a 4pt spacing scale and limit heading styles to three sizes tied to hero, section, and body copy.

principles.title: Brand without bloat
principles.definition: Use brand flourishes only when they support comprehension or trust, never as decoration.
principles.whyItMatters: Decorative flourishes compete with proof or CTAs and sap load speed.
principles.example: Swap heavy background illustrations for a subtle gradient that still points toward the form.

principles.title: Accessibility-grade contrast
principles.definition: All interactive elements meet WCAG AA contrast and have obvious hover or focus states.
principles.whyItMatters: Low contrast CTAs and form labels tank conversions for mobile and low-vision visitors.
principles.example: Primary CTA uses #16DB65 on #04121F with a 2px focus outline.

principles.title: Motion with intent
principles.definition: Animations communicate state changes or guide attention, never exist as ornamental loops.
principles.whyItMatters: Frivolous motion distracts from copy and can even trigger nausea for sensitive visitors.
principles.example: Use a subtle opacity fade on testimonial cards instead of autoplaying carousels.

pageTypes.title: UX
pageTypes.description: Map flows, heuristics, and instrumentation to guarantee each click feels obvious.

prompts.name: Channel Don Norman
prompts.shortDescription: Human-centered design author who obsesses over affordances, mapping, and feedback loops.
prompts.prompt: Act as Don Norman running heuristics on this flow. Pinpoint where visibility, feedback, or control breaks down, then prescribe interface tweaks and microcopy to restore confidence.

prompts.name: Channel Steve Krug
prompts.shortDescription: Don't Make Me Think author who insists every click feels obvious without user manuals.
prompts.prompt:
**Channel Steve Krug from Dont Make Me Think**
Refactor this page using his core UX principles.

You are refactoring the provided page. Apply these rules while keeping the existing logic and behavior:

1. Make everything obvious. Remove anything that forces the user to think.
2. Reduce cognitive load. Improve hierarchy, spacing, grouping, and clarity.
3. Make the first click feel correct. Surface the primary action.
4. Use common conventions. Avoid reinventing patterns.
5. Ensure the page instantly answers three questions:
   Where am I
   What can I do here
   How do I move forward or back
6. Remove unnecessary words and simplify copy.
7. Keep navigation predictable and clearly marked.
8. Make interactive elements obviously clickable.
9. Limit choices to what the user needs right now.
10. Structure the layout for scanning with headings and visual grouping.
11. Suggest small usability improvements if something feels confusing or inconsistent.

Your task: Rewrite the JSX, layout, components, class structure, headings, labels, and overall UX so the page follows these principles without changing any core functionality.

prompts.name: Channel Jared Spool
prompts.shortDescription: UIE founder who backs every UX bet with observation, research, and iterative learning loops.
prompts.prompt: Act as Jared Spool evaluating activation. Map the minimum happy path, remove detours, and note the instrumentation needed to watch real users complete the task.

prompts.name: Channel Julie Zhuo
prompts.shortDescription: Product leadership voice who turns ambiguous requirements into confident first-use journeys.
prompts.prompt: Act as Julie Zhuo storyboarding this product experience. Describe each screen's job, the proof or reassurance it must provide, and the signals that show a user is ready for the next action.

principles.title: State transparency
principles.definition: Every interaction confirms what just happened, what is next, and how long it takes.
principles.whyItMatters: Ambiguous states spike support tickets and make users abandon flows before converting.
principles.example: Add inline validation and progress summaries to multistep forms.

principles.title: Momentum loops
principles.definition: Each step tees up the next action with context, proof, or a preview of the reward.
principles.whyItMatters: Dead-end screens stall motivation and make users question why they started.
principles.example: After selecting a template, immediately preview the filled hero so the CTA feels within reach.

principles.title: Guardrails, not roadblocks
principles.definition: Prevent mistakes early with guidance while always offering a way to recover.
principles.whyItMatters: Hard errors force users to restart flows and inflate bounce rates.
principles.example: Inline hints highlight acceptable file types before upload instead of showing an error afterward.

principles.title: Device parity
principles.definition: Critical actions stay equally clear on mobile, tablet, and desktop.
principles.whyItMatters: Paid traffic skews mobile; if the CTA or nav is buried, sessions die instantly.
principles.example: Surface sticky CTA bars on mobile once the hero scrolls out of view.
